items.bold: GHALIBAF: Iran will CLOSE Hormuz again if US does not lift blockade.
items.text: Iran Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf posted on X Friday evening: Iran would close the Strait of Hormuz if the US does not lift its blockade of Iranian ports. This is the most critical new risk since the Hormuz opening was declared. The Hormuz opening by FM Araghchi is explicitly conditional — tied to Lebanon ceasefire AND implicitly to blockade lifting. Trump has said blockade remains "in full force" until deal is 100% complete. The gap between Iran's condition (lift blockade) and US condition (full deal signed) creates a dangerous window before April 22. If second round talks stall this weekend, Ghalibaf threat could become reality.

items.bold: RUBIO: Iran CAN have civilian nuclear energy program — major US position softening.
items.text: Secretary of State Marco Rubio on April 18 said Iran can have a civilian nuclear energy program instead of a military WMD atomic weapons program. This is a significant softening from the US position of "no enrichment at all." It creates a potential landing zone: Iran suspends weapons-grade enrichment, accepts IAEA oversight of civilian program, and transfers or dilutes 440kg HEU. Rubio also urged European countries to quickly reimpose sanctions on Iran, warning Iran is nearing nuclear weapons capability — keeping the pressure track active alongside the diplomatic track.

For India: Brent at $88-90 vs pre-Hormuz-open $95+ is direct relief. LPG price cut mechanism: if Brent holds below $85 for 2+ weeks, OMCs have headroom to cut cylinder price. items.bold: Second round talks this WEEKEND — Trump said Saturday/Sunday in Islamabad.

items.bold: Hegseth vs Waltz: US divided on attacking Iran militarily.
items.text: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and National Security Advisor Mike Waltz reportedly divided on whether US military should attack Iran. Also said US would "lead the pack" in possibly attacking and there are only two alternatives: "bombing them viciously or nicely" — undecided. Internal US split is actually positive for diplomacy: Waltz representing dovish track, Hegseth the hawkish. Trump playing both for maximum pressure.

assessment.body:
Day 50 brings two developments that define the next 96 hours.

THE RUBIO CONCESSION — CIVILIAN NUCLEAR IS ON THE TABLE
• Rubio April 18: Iran can have a civilian nuclear energy program
• This is the most significant US concession since the war began
• Previous US position: effectively zero enrichment
• New landing zone: Iran suspends weapons-grade enrichment (60%+) + IAEA oversight + HEU transfer
• Pakistan and Iran had already surfaced HEU options: third country or dilute to 3%
• Araghchi: Iran was "inches away from an MoU" at Islamabad — this concession may close the gap
• Rubio simultaneously pushed Europe to reimpose sanctions — dual-track pressure + concession

THE GHALIBAF THREAT — THE NEW CRITICAL RISK
• Ghalibaf Friday evening: Iran will close Hormuz if US does not lift blockade
• Hormuz opening by Araghchi was explicitly "in line with Lebanon ceasefire"
• Ghalibaf is adding a second condition: blockade must be lifted
• Trump: blockade "in full force" until deal 100% complete
• This creates a 4-day window where both sides are in a dangerous standoff
• If second round talks this weekend produce a framework: blockade lifted → Hormuz stays open
• If talks stall: Ghalibaf threat could be activated before April 22

THE SECOND ROUND — THIS WEEKEND IN ISLAMABAD
• Trump Friday: talks could happen this weekend
• Nuclear gap: US wants 20-year enrichment pause, Iran offered 5-year
• Rubio civilian-nuclear concession creates middle ground
• Araghchi said Iran was "inches away" at Islamabad — both sides know how close they are
• Pakistan preparing logistics; Munir heading to Washington to brief first
• Key unknowns: delegation level, whether Ghalibaf attends, Lebanon disarmament clause

INDIA — THE WEEKEND SCORECARD (DAY 50)
• Sensex 78,494 (+505 Apr 17): just 205 pts from pre-war high of 78,699
• Brent ~$88-90: down 9% from pre-Hormuz-open levels
• LPG cut threshold: ~$85 sustained × 2 weeks = full Rs 853/cylinder cut
• Week gain: Sensex recovered 1,647 pts in 3 trading sessions Apr 14-17
• FII turning structural buyers (Rs 382 Cr Apr 16)
• Next trading: Monday April 21 — ceasefire expiry day itself

WHAT TO WATCH THIS WEEKEND
• Official confirmation of second round Islamabad talks
• Iran formal response to Rubio civilian-nuclear concession
• Whether Ghalibaf or Araghchi sets the Iranian tone
• Brent movement Saturday/Sunday — sustained below $85 = LPG cut confirmed
• Any Lebanon flashpoint that could activate Ghalibaf threat

CEASEFIRE: APRIL 22 — 4 DAYS
